screens-add-position.description:
Add Position screen (Linear SHO-27, "Screen: Add flow") — first built 2026-10-08, redesigned
2026-10-11, and **rebuilt 2026-10-13 to Shoham's "Create position flow" in Figma (node
302:2265)**, four frames left to right: empty → URL filled → Create position pressed →
Position details revealed.

**What the 2026-10-13 frames changed** (from the user's screenshots + the frame's layout
metadata; per-node styles for most of the screen could not be pulled — Figma MCP quota — so
type sizes below for the header are matched to the measured heights, see "Not from Figma"):
  - No Header Bar / back arrow any more — the screen opens straight on the "Start here"
    headline. `onBack` is gone; navigation is the Bottom Nav (Add is the current item).
  - Copy: "Start here" / "The right door often looks like just another tab." (was "Start
    here." / "Paste the link below — you never know where it'll lead."), field label "Paste
    the job posting URL here", trailing clipboard icon, "How did I apply?", "Save details".
  - **"Fetch details" (a Secondary Button) became "Create position" (a Primary Button)** with a
    sync icon that turns while the sync runs — Shoham's explicit ask. The button keeps its
    Default look while busy (see PrimaryButton's `loading`).
  - The details block (divider → "Position details" → Company, Role, How did I apply?, Save
    details) appears below the URL group once the sync resolves. Company and Role are
    auto-filled; How did I apply? is left for the person to choose, per the brief.
  - Groups are 48px apart (`--spacing-flow-gap`), fields 16px apart, label-to-field 4px.
  - "Required" tags are gone from the fields. Save is still gated on URL + Company + Role.

**Decisions made without asking, easy to reverse:**
  - **The "Or enter the details yourself" link is removed** — the frames don't have it. That
    was this screen's only manual path (design-brief.md §5: Company "typed if fetch fails").
    While the fetch is a stub that never fails, nothing is lost; a real fetch will need a
    failure path, which should be designed then rather than kept as an orphan link now.
  - **Create position is disabled while the URL is empty** (the Primary Button's locked
    Disabled look). Figma frame 1 shows it fully purple with an empty field; pressing it with
    nothing to sync would do nothing, so it's disabled rather than a dead-looking active
    button. One-line change if the literal frame is wanted.
  - **The three-stage FetchingIndicator text stays** under the button while the icon spins
    (it was requested 2026-10-12 and the new frames don't mention removing it). Drop the
    `{fetching && <FetchingIndicator />}` line to go icon-only.
  - **The clipboard icon is wired up** to paste from the clipboard (the frames only show it).
    Where the browser won't allow clipboard reads — notably plain-HTTP origins, like opening
    the dev build over a LAN IP — it says so under the field instead of silently doing
    nothing.
  - The auto-fill is still the same fixed stub ("Acme Corp" / "Senior Product Designer"), and
    the "demo data — real fetch not wired up yet" disclosure under the URL field stays even
    though the Figma frame doesn't show it: the data is fake and shouldn't pass as real.

**Not from Figma:** the header's type styles (28px/700 display for the title; 14px/600
body-strong for the subtext — matched to the frame's 31px and 20px text heights), the
clipboard/chevron icon size (20, measured from the screenshots), and everything about the
Bottom Nav beyond its 393x57 box. See BottomNav's doc comment.

Swapping in a real fetch now means passing `onFetch` (the stub is just its default).

**2026-10-15 — app shell, phase A: the fetch can fail, and the screen has four states.**
Source: `briefs/app-shell.md` §4 (Shoham's decisions), `design-briefs/app-shell-states.md`
§3.5, canvas artboards 08 and 09. The earlier "Calls made" about the removed manual-entry link
(item 2 above) is closed by this: the failed fetch is the manual path.
  - **idle** — URL only; details hidden. **fetching** — the existing FetchingIndicator.
  - **fetched-success** — details revealed and autofilled; **Create position is DISABLED**, so
    Save details is the only call to action (Shoham, comment on artboard 09). This reverses
    the 2026-10-13 behavior, where it stayed enabled.
  - **fetched-failed** — details revealed EMPTY, a note line under Create position ("Couldn't
    read that link. Add the details below."), Create position stays ENABLED so retrying is
    pressing it again. Focus is not moved (it would raise the keyboard on a phone). A retry
    that succeeds fills only the fields that are still empty — it never overwrites typing.
  - **Editing the URL**: from success it returns to idle — details hidden, Create position
    enabled, the autofilled Company and Role cleared (the old fetch's data no longer describes
    this URL; How did I apply? is the person's own answer, so it's kept). From failed the
    details stay open, what was typed is kept, and only the note clears.
  - **Save failed** — if `onSave` rejects or throws, the note line "Couldn’t save that. Nothing
    was changed, try again." appears between How did I apply? and Save details; nothing else
    changes and Save stays enabled. It clears when Save is tried again.
The two note lines live in persistent `role="status"` regions so they're announced; an empty
region takes no space. The fetch is injectable (`onFetch`) so a story can show the failure.

Judgment calls (flagged, easy to reverse): the canvas draws 24px between the divider and
"Position details" and between that heading and the first field; this build keeps the
Figma-measured 48px / 16px of the 2026-10-13 frames (decision #23: Figma wins) — the canvas
artboards were not drawn from those frames' metadata. The fetch result is discarded if the URL
is edited while it is still running. Disclosure "demo data" is shown only when the default
stub produced the fill.

**2026-10-22 — the app reads the link locally.** The app now passes an `onFetch` backed by the
pure parser `app/linkDetails.ts` (no network): a link that yields a company opens the existing
fetched-success state with Company (and Role, when the link carries one) filled in, How did I
apply? untouched and Create position disabled, exactly as before; nothing readable is the
existing fetched-failed state. One addition on this screen: when a SUPPLIED `onFetch` actually
filled a field, the note region under Create position says "Filled in from the link. Check the
details." (NoteLine with a `Link2` icon instead of the warning triangle). Calls I made, easy to
reverse: the note sits in the same live region as the failure note (announced once, 16px under
the button); it is not shown when nothing was filled (both fields already typed, after a
failure); it goes when the URL is edited (the fill is cleared then too). The copy is pending
ux-writer review. The default stub (stories only) and its "demo data" line are unchanged. With
a local parse there is no wait, so the FetchingIndicator is not seen in the app (at most a
frame); the screen was not given an artificial delay.

**Later on 2026-10-22 — the live link reader.** The app's `onFetch` now asks Shoham's link reader
(a Cloudflare Worker, up to 6 seconds) before falling back to the local parser
(`app/linkReader.ts`). Nothing on this screen changed: while the reader is awaited the existing
fetching state shows (the three-step FetchingIndicator is seen again), and its answer arrives
through the same success / failure states and the same "Filled in from the link" note.

**2026-10-25 — paste and clear on the job link** (`design-briefs/field-behavior.md`, Shoham's
decisions; strings from `design-briefs/copy-field-behavior.md`). The link field shows the clipboard
(label "Paste job link", was "Paste from clipboard") while empty and an X ("Clear job link") once
filled: one slot, one job. Paste keeps the first link in what was copied (`app/pasteFields.ts`,
which agrees with `linkDetails.ts` on what a link is; no scheme added); text with no link in it is
REFUSED with "No link found in what you copied." (before, any text was taken). The three notes
(empty clipboard, nothing recognised, clipboard unavailable) replace the two old ones, which had an
em dash; a dismissed iOS Paste bubble and a good paste say nothing. A pasted or cleared link goes
through the same change handler as typing, so the link reader flow (Create position, Company and
Role from the link) is unchanged. Nothing is focused after a paste (no keyboard). Also: the link
field asks for the url keyboard, no capitals, no autocorrect; all three fields set autoComplete off
(Company and Role also words / autocorrect off, per the brief's table). Calls I made: the paste
button now has the 44px tap area (`trailingTouchTarget`, icon unmoved) like Edit's date clear;
`readClipboardText` is a test seam. Not seen on a phone (the iOS Paste bubble is a two-tap path).

tsType.name: signature
tsType.raw: (data: { url: string; company: string; role: string; howApplied: string }) => void | Promise<void>

type.name: signature
type.raw: { url: string; company: string; role: string; howApplied: string }

onSave.description:
Called with the form's data. May return a promise; if it rejects (or throws), the screen
shows the save-failed note line and changes nothing else.

onFetch.description:
Replaces the stubbed "Create position" sync. Resolve with the details, reject for a failed
fetch. When omitted the stub runs (fixed "Acme Corp" / "Senior Product Designer") and the
"demo data" disclosure is shown under the URL field; when supplied, it isn't.

onNavigate.description: Bottom Nav taps. The screen marks Add as the current destination.

defaultUrl.description:
Story/demo convenience, matching Card's `defaultExpanded` pattern — lets a story start
with the form already filled in, without needing real navigation state.

defaultRevealed.description:
Story/demo convenience — forces the details open without needing a default Company/Role
value to infer it from (e.g. to show the revealed-but-empty state).

defaultFetchState.description:
Story/demo convenience — starts the screen in a fetch outcome without running a fetch.
`'failed'` shows the note and the empty details; `'success'` shows the details with Create
position disabled. Defaults to `'success'` when `defaultRevealed` or any default Company /
Role / How applied is passed (the previous behavior's closest equivalent), else `'idle'`.

defaultSaveFailed.description: Story/demo convenience — starts with the save-failed note showing.

defaultFilledFromLink.description:
Story/demo convenience — with `defaultFetchState: 'success'`, also shows the "Filled in from
the link" note, as after a supplied `onFetch` filled something in.

Frame 1 of the Create position flow — just the headline, the URL field and "Create
position" (disabled until there's a URL). Type or paste a URL, then press Create position:
the sync icon turns, the staged text plays, and the position details appear below with
Company and Role auto-filled. How did I apply? is left for you to choose, then Save details.
(The fetch itself is a stub — see the component's doc comment.)

2026-10-15 app-shell build the only way to reach this is a failed fetch, so it now shows that

thing; kept so the story list doesn't lose an entry.

Create position is disabled (a fetch has succeeded, so Save details is the one call to
action); edit the URL to see it return to the idle state with the details hidden.

opens EMPTY with the note under the button, Create position stays enabled so retrying is

the URL clears the note but keeps the details open.

molecules-add-step-sheet.name: AddStepSheet
molecules-add-step-sheet.description:
Add a step sheet — Add a step, Part B (2026-11-04), built from `design-briefs/stage-advance.md`
(sections 2 to 5, 9, 10), `design-briefs/copy-stage-advance.md` (every string, curly apostrophes)
and `briefs/stage-advance.md` section 4 ("One field decides the path", "Thinking moment", "Typed
text is kept as a draft"). On `ConfirmationSheet`, the way `ReasonSheet` is. Code-only: the canvas
page "Add a step" was not opened here, and no Linear ticket was checked.

One field. Chips fill it (", " between). About 400 ms after she stops typing the text is read on the
phone (`app/splitSteps.ts`): ONE step shows a required "When" (today), TWO OR MORE show "N steps
found · dates can wait" and "Review N steps", then a review list in the same sheet. Over 20 says so
and the primary stays disabled. While the pause runs, "Reading what you wrote…" shows with three
pulsing dots (static under reduced motion), announced through the sheet's one `role="status"`
region, which also carries the found line, the notes and the failure line.

Failure: the sheet stays, everything typed stays, the line for the error shows. Archived and gone
disable the primary ("Not now" is the way out). A second press while saving does nothing (`busy`).
Like ReasonSheet, the form is a child of the sheet, so its state resets every time the sheet closes
and reopens; the caller hands the kept draft back as `initialText`.

Calls I made (judgment, easy to change; the briefs were silent): a row's type word is left out when it
would only repeat the row's own label ("Interview" beside "Interview"); the sheet's title stays "Add a
step" and the review list has its own "Check your steps" heading under it (focus lands there); in the
review list the secondary button reads "Back" instead of "Not now" (Escape and the scrim still
close, and the text is kept as a draft); "Add date" is the native date field itself, laid
transparently over the words "Add date" (a tap opens the phone's date picker at once; no extra
tap), and a dated row gets a "Clear date" button; the remove button is a trash icon, the date clear
an X; a chip tap reads at once (no pause); tapping a chip whose word is already in the field adds
it again ("interview, interview" is two rounds); the stage change cross-fades by fading the new
stage IN only (no fade out); the When field fades in and disappears instantly (opacity only, no
height animation, as asked); a row's date outside 2000 to 2100 disables "Add N steps" (the data
layer would refuse it) with no message; the multiline field keeps its 96px minimum (the design says
two lines; the component's token is three); the notes use an info icon, the failure line the
warning triangle. NOT verified on a phone: the keyboard over the sheet, the native date picker
opened from the overlay, Safari's form bar.

screens-archive.name: ArchiveScreen
screens-archive.description:
Archive screen — built 2026-10-19 from `briefs/archive.md` (UI slice, boards A, C, D of the
canvas "Archive"). Props-driven: no store, no router, no toast. Header "Archive" (same type as
"Your stack", no count), a full-width filter, a flat list of `ArchiveRow`s, the Bottom Nav with
Archive current.

**Filter** (decision 3): the existing SegmentedControl, four options labelled
`All · 37` / `Rejected · 25` / `Ghosted · 8` / `Other · 4` (a middle dot, counts computed from
`records`), segments 44px tall, on a white track (decision 4, via the control's new
`--segment-track-bg` hook). `Other` is every reason that is not exactly `Rejected` or `Ghosted`.
Hidden when there are no records. Changing the filter closes the open row.

The filter is `scrollable` (Shoham, 2026-10-19, after seeing it on her iPhone): every segment is
padded 12px each side and sized to its content, so the title and count are never cut, and the
track scrolls sideways when the four don't fit (at 393px wide, with the brief's counts, they just
don't). The selected segment is scrolled fully into view. This replaced a shrink-and-ellipsis
version made after QA at 320px.

**Opening** (decision 6): tapping a row replaces it, in place, with the full Card in archived
mode (see Card's `onRestore`), so any other open row closes; Show less puts the row back. The
page scrolls; nothing is clipped. Focus moves to the opened card and returns to the row on
close. After Restore, focus goes to the next row's button
(else the previous one, else the filter, else the header) once the parent has removed the record.
No animation, so there is nothing to gate for reduced motion.

**Empty** (decision 10): `Nothing archived yet` with no button and no filter; a filter that
matches nothing shows the same block headed `Nothing here` (same body line — a literal reading
of "the same empty block"; reversible).

Calls I made: the header is its own `h1` styled like the Stack's, not `HeaderBar` (that one has
a back arrow); the row's second line is the role, else `Applied <date>`; the screen promotes the
last reached pipeline step to `current` for the card (see `endedAt`); a record's own
`onOpenLink` is what enables "Open original link" — the data mapping produces no link yet, so
the wiring (B2) has to supply one. Spacing between header, filter and list (16px) is a guess.
Not seen in a browser by the author.

**2026-10-22, TEMPORARY: `onOpenBackupTemp`.** A mockup aid (Shoham: "we will not keep" it): the
home-screen app has no address bar, so the Backup page could not be reached. When the prop is
passed, `TempBackupLink` ("Backup and restore") is drawn centred below the list's last row (16px
under it) and below the empty block's body line, in both the "Nothing archived yet" and the
filtered "Nothing here" versions (my call: the brief names the empty state, and the filtered one
is the same block). It sits inside `<main>`, so it scrolls with the list; it is not in the
Bottom Nav. Remove with the prop when the real settings screen exists.

(same idea as `editUnavailable`).

Archive tab (2026-10-19). **Giving this prop turns the card into an archived card**: the
actions become Show less, Open original link, Restore to stack (no Edit, no Archive), the
Termination block moves up to sit right after the header, the pipeline rows stop being
tappable, and the empty-data cases below are hidden rather than drawn bare. Restore is a
normal secondary button, not danger (briefs/archive.md decision 8). Absent, the card is
exactly what it always was. The caller removes the card after this fires; the Card itself
shows no toast and asks for no confirmation (decision 9).

record the data layer could not read (position-card-states.md 3.7, artboard 09): a "?" tile,
the title, one line with a warning icon, and a "Copy saved data" button. Every other prop is
ignored. `copyText` is the record exactly as stored; `copyable: false` (the value could not be
turned into text) disables the button. There is no Remove here: removing a record needs a data
operation that does not exist yet (step 2b).

hiring-process section title reads `Hiring process · reached <label>` (was `Pipeline`, until 2026-11-04). Independent of `onRestore`.

molecules-bottom-nav.description:
Bottom Nav — built in code 2026-10-13. It exists in Figma (SHO-18, with Nav Item SHO-7 and Nav
Add Button SHO-8) but was never translated; this is the first code version, made for the
"Create position" flow whose frames each show it (instance 302:2294).

**What's confirmed vs. inferred — read this before trusting it.** The Figma MCP quota ran out
before this instance's own styles could be pulled, so:
  - *From the frame metadata (exact):* 393x57 across the bottom edge of the screen.
  - *From the user's screenshots (measured, not read from Figma):* five icon-only items (decision
    #9 — no labels), the Add item a dark rounded square with a white plus, the others in
    tertiary gray, a 1px top border on a surface fill. The 8px padding / 16px gap / item size
    was the arithmetic that reproduced the 57px height and the icons' horizontal positions.
  - *Guessed:* icon identities — `Copy` for Stack (two overlapping rounded squares in the
    screenshot; the Figma file's icon names are literal Lucide names, so this is the closest
    match, not a confirmed one) — the Add fill (`--color-nav-add-bg`, gray-700, matched by eye),
    the active tint (`color/text/primary`), and the pressed treatment.
  - *Deviation from the frames, decided 2026-10-15:* Dashboard is dimmed (`--opacity-disabled`)
    and disabled, as design-brief.md §1 says ("coming soon"). The frames show it undimmed.

**Made bigger 2026-10-19 (Archive brief, decision 12 — Shoham, "feels right" on the phone).**
Bar 64px (was 57), items 48px tall (was 40), Add button 48x48 (was 40x40), nav icons 26px (was
24) and the plus 22px (was 20). Driven by `--size-nav-item` (40 -> 48). Why: the 40px items
broke the project's own 44px `--size-touch-target`. The icon sizes are literals in this file as
before (there is no icon-size token). CALL I MADE: the brief says "64px" but also "8 + 48 + 8
+ 1px border", which adds to 65. Its other derived numbers (Toast 80 = 64 + 16, "3px higher"
= 7 / 2) all assume 64, and Figma-wins, so the bar is 64 with the border drawn inside the top
8px (`padding-top: 8px - 1px`). If 65 was meant, change that one padding and the `+ 1px` that
StackScreen's `--stack-nav-height` no longer carries.

Needs a Figma pass (node 302:2294 and the Nav Item / Nav Add Button components) when quota
allows. Icon-only, so each item carries an `aria-label`.

molecules-card.name: Card
molecules-card.description:
Card (Linear SHO-17, now also SHO-26) — the Stack screen's front-of-card, which as of
2026-10-05 also owns its own expanded ("Tap-in") state. Rebuilt the same day, per Shoham's
updated Figma mock and the discussion that followed: there is no separate Tap-in screen
(see design-brief.md §4, retitled "Expanded card") — the "Show more details" button
toggles this same card between collapsed and expanded in place, and swaps its own label to
"Show less". That button is the ONLY way to trigger the toggle — tapping the card elsewhere
keeps its existing stack-browse meaning only and never changes expand state. This was an
open question as of the first pass at this redesign; Shoham closed it out explicitly
(two gestures doing the same thing felt confusing) — see SHO-17.

Collapsed content is unchanged from the original Card build, translated from Figma node
142:1262: header, Progress Bar, Signal Chip, Location/Office days Meta Items.

Expanded content was built code-first 2026-10-05, then re-aligned 2026-10-07 to match
Shoham's own Figma build of this same card (node 226:743), which is now the source of
truth per her instruction — Figma wins on drift, code changes to match it. Current shape,
in order: Pipeline (full step list — replaces the mini Progress Bar while expanded, see the
interpretation note below), Compensation (Asked only, shown as a range — see the
`compensationAsked` prop doc for why "Offered" was dropped), Contact (HR/Hiring Manager
toggle, reusing Segmented Control; icons on email/phone confirmed against Figma 2026-10-07),
Logistics (Location + office days only), Applied (its own section, split out of Logistics
2026-10-07 to match Figma — a uniform-weight date + relative string, plus the "How Applied"
chip, a Signal Chip with its dot hidden). The chip moved from Logistics into Applied
2026-10-08, per Shoham: "how you applied" belongs with "when you applied", not with
location/office-days. Notes, Termination block (conditional), Actions (Show less, then Edit
/ Open original link / Archive — trailing icons, matching Figma's convention elsewhere in
the system; Archive uses the new `danger` SecondaryButton variant Shoham added in Figma).
"Show less" is now the same SecondaryButton as the other three (2026-10-08, Shoham's
explicit call) — it had briefly been a lighter plain-text treatment (Claude's own
non-blocking suggestion on SHO-41), which Figma never adopted; all four Action buttons now
render as one uniform stack, same as "Show more details" looks in the collapsed state.

One interpretation call, not yet confirmed by Shoham, worth flagging: expanding REPLACES
the collapsed summary row (Progress Bar + Signal Chip + Location/Office days) with the
fuller sections, rather than showing both — Pipeline and Logistics already carry that same
information in more detail, so showing both looked redundant. Easy to change if that read
is wrong.

**Archived card, added 2026-10-19 (Archive tab, briefs/archive.md decisions 7 and 8).** Three
additive props: `onRestore` (its presence IS the archived mode), `pipelineReached` (the
Pipeline title becomes `Pipeline · reached <label>`) and, in archived mode, a ` · ended here`
suffix on the label of the step whose state is `current` (the caller decides which step that
is; ArchiveScreen promotes the last reached step). In archived mode, and only then: the
Termination block sits right after the header instead of after Notes; the actions are Show
less / Open original link (disabled, labelled `No link saved`, when `onOpenLink` is absent) /
Restore to stack (counter-clockwise arrow, a normal secondary button); pipeline rows are not
tappable; the company and role stop at two lines (QA, 2026-10-19); and an empty role is left
out instead of drawn as an empty line. With none of the new props the archived-only behaviour
does not apply.

**Phase B step 2a, 2026-10-19 (before real data is shown; briefs/app-shell-phase-b2a.md).**
Three changes, for EVERY card: (1) an unset `howAppliedIndex` no longer defaults to 0 ("Cold"):
with no value the Applied section shows the date and no chip (33 of the 45 real records have no
known `howApplied`). Cards that pass an index render exactly as before. (2) An empty `location`
or `officeDays` is not drawn: its Meta Item is omitted entirely (no bare icon), and the whole
meta row / Logistics section goes when both are empty. Cards with both render as before.
(3) New prop `unreadable` turns the card into the "Couldn't read this one" card for a stored
record the data layer could not read (position-card-states.md 3.7): "?" tile, the title, a
warning line, and a Copy saved data button (label becomes "Copied" for 2s; a clipboard that
refuses shows "Couldn't copy from this address..."). It draws no depth layers (they are a fixed
287px and this card is about 216px, so they would show below it) and has no Remove: removing a
record needs a data operation that does not exist yet (step 2b). Also `restoreUnavailable`
(archived mode): "Restore to stack" is drawn disabled until Restore exists. Not seen on a phone
by the author; the headless run is in the status doc.

**2026-10-19, after QA of step 2a.** On an expanded, non-archived card, "Open original link" is
now disabled and reads `No link saved` when `onOpenLink` is absent (it used to be an enabled
button that did nothing; stories without the callback change accordingly). `editUnavailable` /
`archiveUnavailable` draw Edit / Archive disabled in place (Shoham's call: disabled, not hidden,
until step 2b); Archive keeps its danger border and text, the disabled fill is what shows it is
off. Absent, they behave as before.

**2026-10-25 — Edit position, Part B (copy: `design-briefs/copy-edit-position.md` 1.7).** New
`hasDraft`: the Edit button reads "Continue editing" with the accessible name "Continue editing,
not saved yet", on the Stack card and the archived card. The archived card gains Edit as its
second action (Show less, Edit, Open original link, Restore to stack), drawn only when `onEdit`
or `editUnavailable` is given, so archived cards without either are exactly as before; a twin
or unreadable card keeps it disabled (`editUnavailable`). The work model reaches the card
through the existing `officeDays` slot (the mapping puts "Remote" / "Hybrid" / "On-site" there);
the prop keeps its old name, only what the data layer fills it with changed.

**2026-11-04 — Add a step, Part B** (`design-briefs/stage-advance.md` sections 3 and 12). The
section heading "Pipeline" is now "Hiring process" (the Archive's line reads
"Hiring process · reached <label>"; display only). New `onAddStep` / `stepsUnavailable`: a
leading-plus SecondaryButton "Add a step" under the rows, on an expanded non-archived card, and the
section is drawn with just that button when the card has no steps. A row is a button only if it
has an `eventId` (the app added it) and `onAdvanceStep` is given; before, every non-done row was
tappable and nothing happened. Row kinds are in `PipelineStepRow`. Flag: the section's rows and
button sit in one `<section>`; the gap between them is the section's own gap (a guess).

Supersedes `TapInDetailView` (job-tracker-ui/src/components/TapInDetailView), which modeled
this as a separate full-screen component with its own Header Bar. That component is now
stale and kept only as a section-level content reference — see its own file header.

molecules-confirmation-sheet.name: ConfirmationSheet
molecules-confirmation-sheet.description:
Confirmation Sheet (Linear SHO-24) — built 2026-10-15 (app shell, phase A). SHO-24 was listed
as "Screen-level, not started" with no Figma node, so this is the first version, drawn from
`design-briefs/app-shell-states.md` §3.6 and canvas artboards 07 and 10–13. Linear itself was
not checked (no connector here), so a locked spec on SHO-24 could still differ.

CONFIRMED by Shoham (canvas review, 2026-10-15): full width, anchored to the bottom and
covering the Bottom Nav; fill `color/bg/surface`; top corners `radius/card` (28px); padding 24
on the sides and top, 24 + 34 at the bottom; a scrim of `color/text/primary` at 40% behind it;
no drag handle (it would imply a drag-to-dismiss nobody specified) and no close button (the
composition's "Keep it" is the exit).

Mine, not from the design: the bottom padding is 24 + `max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 34px)`
so a real inset wins where the platform reports one and the drawn 34 holds elsewhere; the
focus handling below; the motion timings (the motion tokens themselves are still "proposed").

Behavior: `role="dialog"` `aria-modal`, labelled by its title. Focus moves to the first
focusable control inside (the panel itself if there is none), is trapped (Tab wraps; focus
that escapes is pulled back), Escape and the scrim call `onClose`, and focus returns to
whatever had it when the sheet opened — the Archive button, for the Archive action. A
pull-down entry has no focused opener, so when that is built it will need to hand the sheet an
element to return to. Rises with `--duration-base` / `--ease-out`, leaves in `--duration-fast`;
under `prefers-reduced-motion` it is an opacity fade with no travel.

Placement: `position: fixed`, so it covers the viewport; render it anywhere in the screen
(it is not portalled). The on-screen keyboard: the root follows the visual viewport, so the
panel sits on top of the keyboard and scrolls when needed (2026-11-04, after her phone test). The content behind is not made `inert` — aria-modal covers screen readers, the focus
trap covers keyboards.

atoms-dropdown.name: Dropdown
atoms-dropdown.description:
Dropdown (brand-new atom, built 2026-10-11) — no Figma node and no Linear ticket exist for
this yet. It replaces Segmented Control (SHO-14) for the Add Position screen's "How Applied"
field specifically, per Shoham's direct feedback: three equal-weight segmented buttons for an
optional, rarely-filled field read as more visual commitment than the field deserves — a
single tappable row that opens a real picker feels lighter. This does NOT touch how "How
Applied" is *displayed* read-only on the expanded Card — that's still the Signal-Chip-based
chip added 2026-10-08 (decision #23), untouched by this change. Segmented Control itself isn't
retired; it's just no longer this field's input.

Built as a real native <select>, not a custom-rendered popover/listbox — gets free keyboard
nav, screen-reader semantics, and correct mobile picker behavior (the iOS/Android wheel
picker) for nothing, the same reasoning that kept Text Input Field a real <input>. The select
is visually transparent; the chrome around it (border, height, radius, background, label) is
a styled wrapper plus a decorative chevron icon, so it reads as part of this app's component
family rather than a bare OS control.

Visual chrome was originally copied from Text Input Field (SHO-13)'s own locked spec —
`radius/chip`, 52px height, `spacing/section-gap` horizontal padding — for family
consistency, with nothing locking it for THIS component.

**2026-10-13:** a real Figma node now exists for this — the "How did I apply?" Input Field
instance in the Create position flow (302:2308), read directly. It confirms the chrome
(14px radius, 16px padding, 1px default border, surface fill, `type/body` text, trailing
ChevronDown), and corrects two guesses: the label is `type/label` (13px Bold), not
`type/caption`, and the placeholder "Please select" is `color/text/primary`, not dimmed
tertiary. Still no Linear ticket for Dropdown itself.

**2026-10-25 — Edit position:** optional `emptyLabel` (a real first option with an empty value,
so a choice can be cleared: the design brief's "gap"), `selectId` and `onBlur`. Without them the
placeholder behaves as before. A value that is not one of the options shows the empty option.

screens-edit-position.name: EditPositionScreen
screens-edit-position.description:
Edit position screen (2026-10-25). Every value here is invented (example.test addresses, 555-01xx
numbers). The stories are also the component tests: most carry a `play` that drives the screen and
checks what it promises (draft kept on leave, the toast only when true, validation on changed
fields only, conflict notes, archived edit, locked fields). The screen never touches storage, so
`onDraft` / `onSave` are spies here.

reactDocgen.description:
Edit position screen — built 2026-10-25 (Edit position, Part B). Sources, in order: `briefs/
edit-position.md` (binding), `design-briefs/copy-edit-position.md` section 1 (every string, copied
from its table; the copy file wins), `design-briefs/edit-position.md` sections 3 to 11. Canvas
page "Edit position" was not opened.

A full-screen form that looks like the Add screen (same background, 20px side margin, 16px
between fields, 48px between groups), filled from the STORED record's values (`saved`, from
`editableValues`), never from the Card. It owns its form state; the caller supplies the saved
values and does the writes (`onDraft`, `onSave`), so the screen itself never touches storage.

States: pristine (Save disabled, no Discard); draft (the status line "Draft kept · not saved
yet", the same for a fresh and a reopened draft, with its row's height always reserved so nothing
jumps; Save enabled; Discard draft); draft that could not be stored (the note replaces the line);
saving (Save turns, every field disabled; "Saving…" only after half a second); save failed; per-field
validation (changed fields only, on blur and on Save); changed meanwhile ("Saved now: …" under each
field changed in both places, the top note, Save then keeps hers); archived / restored meanwhile
(only noticed while the screen is open); position gone (fields and Save disabled, Copy my
changes); discard sheet; leave sheet ONLY when the draft could not be stored. Leaving otherwise
keeps the draft and tells the caller `draftKept` so the toast is only said when true.

Draft timing (design brief section 5): written 500ms after the last change, at once on the first
change (so the status line is true when it appears), on blur, when the tab is hidden, on pagehide
and when the screen goes away.

Calls I made (easy to reverse): locked fields (stored value not text) are disabled with no
message, as no copy exists; the contact "needs a name" rule runs when any field of that slot
changed; Discard draft is disabled in the "no longer there" state; "Copy my changes" copies the
changed fields as `Label: value` lines and says nothing if the clipboard refuses; the date field
has no EP-V-DATE check (a browser date input gives a full date or nothing; it cannot be told
apart from empty); Return moves to the next field and never saves; "Saved now" values are cut at
40 characters; the Bottom Nav marks the Archive when she came from there.

QA fixes, 2026-10-25: the screen writes a draft only after THIS mounted screen changed a value
(`dirty`), so mounting and leaving with nothing touched never removes or overwrites a stored draft
(Forward onto Edit used to delete a kept one); a draft given as `initialDraft` counts as kept for
the leave info. In the "no longer there" state leaving reports `draftKept: false` (no card can
reopen the draft, and the copy file has no string for it), and the draft is left alone. Guessed:
nothing new; confirmed by the QA repro scripts t4, t4b, t7, t14.

Re-QA fixes, 2026-10-25: (M2) a screen that mounted with the position missing now gets the stored
draft from the caller (`initialDraft`) and, when the record comes back and nothing was typed here,
rebuilds its session from the saved values AND that draft, so the first keystroke continues the draft
instead of overwriting it. (L3) In the "no longer there" state the fields show the draft's own
values (conflict notes dropped) and Copy copies them; with no draft nothing differs, so the note
and the Copy button are hidden (EP-GONE promises changes to copy; the copy file has no string for
the empty case, so none is invented, a call to confirm).

**2026-10-25, fixes 3.** (a) Mounted with the position gone, the "has a draft" decision and Copy use
the stored draft's own entries (`draftNames`), cleared ones included, so a draft that only clears a
field is shown and copies "Notes: ". (b) Gone with no draft shows the top note EP-GONE-EMPTY ("This
position is no longer in your saved positions.", no Copy), approved by Shoham 2026-10-25; this
replaces the earlier "show nothing" call above.

**2026-10-25, paste and clear** (`design-briefs/field-behavior.md` "Decided", strings from
`design-briefs/copy-field-behavior.md`). The job link and each contact's email and phone show a
clipboard button while empty ("Paste job link", "Paste HR email", ...) and an X once filled ("Clear
..."); other text fields get neither (the date's own clear stays). A paste is a normal change
(`set`/`update`: draft written, validation only on changed fields; locked and saving fields have
disabled buttons). Clean-up and the notes live in `app/pasteFields.ts`; notes sit under the field as
a NoteLine and go at its next edit. "Name <email>" fills Name only if it is empty. Nothing is
focused after a paste or a clear. Also set the brief's autoCorrect off on Company, Role, Location,
Referred by and Asked (and capitals off on Asked). Calls I made: a refused read (the iOS Paste
bubble dismissed) leaves the field and any old note untouched but removes the old note; a paste
that finishes after the field was filled meanwhile is dropped; the paste notes are not in a live
region (like the validation notes here), they are linked with aria-describedby.

Not verified on a phone: the native date input in the field chrome, the phone keypads, focus
into view with the keyboard open, the Confirmation Sheet over the keyboard.

molecules-fetching-indicator.name: FetchingIndicator
molecules-fetching-indicator.description:
Fetching Indicator — built 2026-10-12. Replaces the flat "Fetching details…" helper text that
the Add Position screen showed under the URL field while the (still stubbed) fetch ran.

**Why:** a single static line reads as "stuck"; three short beats read as the system actively
doing something. This is still entirely part of the fetch *stub* — no network call happens,
and the post-reveal "demo data — real fetch not wired up yet" disclosure stays exactly as it
was. The copy is playful, so it must never be mistaken for evidence of real work.

**Behavior:** advances through the stages on a timer and then *holds* on the last one — it is
deliberately not tied to how long the fetch takes, so a real fetch can replace the stub later
without retuning anything here (a fast one just unmounts it early, a slow one waits on the
final line instead of looping).

**Motion** (built against the `animate` skill's rules): the icon pops with a small overshoot
(CSS keyframes — this sequence is predetermined and non-interruptible, and needs a defined
overshoot a plain transition can't give); the text crossfades and slides up. All three stages
stay mounted and stacked in one grid cell, so swaps are transitions on `data-state` rather
than remounts. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it falls back to a plain opacity
crossfade — no scale, no travel.

**Accessibility:** the animated lines are `aria-hidden`; a single `role="status"` line
announces "Fetching details…" once, so a screen reader isn't read three lines in two seconds.
Mounting a live region together with its content isn't announced reliably by every screen
reader — worth a real-device check, not verified here.

molecules-header-bar.description:
Header Bar (Linear SHO-23) — back arrow + title + trailing action(s). Shared across Tap-in,
Add flow, Search, and Archive (one component, not rebuilt per screen) per the ticket, though
only the Tap-in detail view (SHO-26) uses it so far.

Built directly in code 2026-10-04 — no Figma node exists yet for this component (unlike the
Card family, which was translated from a live Figma build). Shoham asked to keep working in
code rather than spend Figma MCP calls building it there first, so this is built straight from
the ticket + design-brief.md §4.1 ("back, company + role, link to posting, edit/more") and the
existing token set — worth a look in Figma whenever it's built there, same as any other
code-first component.

The ticket only names one token pair (`type/heading-sm` / `color/text/primary`), for what it
calls "title" — company + role is two lines, so this follows the Card's own locked header
hierarchy (decision #14: company name primary/bold, role secondary) rather than inventing a
new pattern. Back/link/more icons (ChevronLeft/ExternalLink/MoreVertical) are a reasonable
Lucide pick for a code-only component, not a literal read of a Figma layer name.

atoms-note-line.name: NoteLine
atoms-note-line.description:
Note Line — added 2026-10-15 (app shell, phase A), code-only: no Figma node, no Linear ticket.

The plain one-line failure/heads-up note that `design-briefs/app-shell-states.md` §3.5 and §3.6
specify and canvas artboards 08, 09 and 13 draw: a 16px `TriangleAlert` plus a sentence in
`type/body`, both `color/text/secondary`. No tint, no box, no border — the icon and the words
carry the state, because the system has no danger/error color (status doc "Still open").
Used for "Couldn't read that link…", "Couldn't save that…" (Add and the reason sheet).

Why not Meta Item: it is the same shape but its text is `nowrap`, and a failure sentence has to
be allowed to wrap at larger text sizes (§3.5). Why not `TextInputField.helperText`: that is
`color/text/tertiary` (about 3.1:1), too faint for a failure.

It carries no live-region role itself. A live region only announces content inserted into an
element that already exists, so the CALLER keeps a persistent `role="status"` element and puts
this inside it — see AddPositionScreen and ReasonSheet.

**2026-10-22: optional `icon`.** The Add screen's "Filled in from the link. Check the details."
is a heads-up, not a failure, so a warning triangle would misread it; the caller passes another
16px icon (it uses `Link2`, my call). Without `icon` the output is unchanged.

molecules-pipeline-step-row.description:

view's Pipeline section. `State` = Done / Current / Upcoming.

outline dot plus the date, and a visually hidden ", upcoming" after the label (SA-L-UPCOMING-AX), so
the meaning never rests on colour. A row with `onClick` is a 44px button (`--size-touch-target`)
with a visible keyboard focus ring. Done is unchanged (check icon). Colours are unchanged:
`color-text-tertiary` is 3.06:1 on white and a separate pass darkens it (decided; this feature
ships no override).

straight off the ticket: `color/status-matched/text` (Done), `color/accent/default` (Current),
`color/text/tertiary` (Upcoming). The Done checkmark and the solid/outline dot distinction are
this component's own interpretation of "dot/checkmark" from the ticket text, not a literal
Figma read — worth comparing once the real component exists there.

screens-post-archive.name: PostArchiveScreen
screens-post-archive.description:
Post-archive screen — built 2026-10-20 from `briefs/post-archive.md` and
`design-briefs/copy-post-archive.md`. What the person sees after Move to Archive has succeeded and
the card has left: a very soft lavender screen, a big phrase that fits the reason, and a snackbar
with the outcome and one action. It covers everything above the Bottom Nav (which stays visible and
usable); it has NO button and no hint text.

**Background.** Built from tokens only, drawn in CSS, no images: a base (`--accent-100` mixed with
the surface color) and four organic shapes in the accent family and the surface color at low
opacity, each blurred with a STATIC `filter: blur()` of 1.5 x `--spacing-stack-gap` (60px, derived;
there is no blur token), strong enough that no shape edge is readable. The shapes do not move (a
drift over the 5-second hold was imperceptible and cost a re-blur every frame); only the whole
screen's opacity animates, in and out.

**Phrase.** `type/display` (28px, 700, tight tracking), `--accent-900` (the deepest accent), centered
about 28% from the top of the area above the nav, with 32px side margins (2 x
`--spacing-section-gap`). Each `\n`-separated part is its own block line with balanced wrapping. The
visible phrase is `aria-hidden`: the phrase and the snackbar text are announced ONCE through a single
polite live region (the Toast is told not to announce itself).

**Ending.** The action (`Done` / `Add a position`), a tap anywhere (including on the snackbar's text), Escape or Enter (Enter on a button
is that button's own click), and after `holdMs` (about 5 seconds; nothing counts down on screen).
Whichever comes first wins; later ones do nothing (a double tap acts
once). The screen fades out (`--duration-base`) and then calls `onClose`; `add` and reduced motion
leave at once. Focus moves to the action button on mount; returning it afterwards is the caller's.

Guessed, not specified: centered text; the phrase's vertical position; the shapes' sizes, positions
and opacities; the fade length. Not seen on a phone by the author.

atoms-primary-button.name: PrimaryButton
atoms-primary-button.description:
Primary Button (Linear SHO-12) — confirmed built in Figma 2026-09-22 (marked Done), the
"Primary" variant of the unified Button component (node 75:48, same component Secondary
Button/SHO-32 translates the "Subtle" variant of). Never translated to code until now.

Built 2026-10-08, code-first: Shoham's call for this Add flow pass (SHO-27) was to work in
code first and sync to Figma later, same pattern as Header Bar and Pipeline Step Row. First
real use: the Add flow's "Save" action — the one primary confirming action against three
outlined Secondary Buttons' worth of visual weight elsewhere in this app; nothing in the
Card/expanded-card work needed a true primary CTA before this.

SHO-13's locked spec (checked only after an initial build guessed `radius/sm`, matching
Secondary Button — wrong, see TextInputField's doc comment for the same lesson) also covers
this component's own ticket, SHO-12, which specs:
  - `State` = `Default` / `Disabled` only — Pressed is NOT locked. SHO-12 itself asks: "does
    this also want the same Pressed treatment as Nav Add Button for tap feedback consistency
    — not specced yet, flag if you add it so Nav Add Button gets updated to match." This
    build adds a :hover/:active → `color/accent/hover` fill anyway (an unusable button with
    no press feedback felt wrong for a real Save action) — flagged on SHO-12 in Linear per
    that instruction, not silently added.
  - Default: `color/accent/default` background, `color/text/on-accent` label — matches.
  - Disabled: `color/bg/surface-sunken` background, `color/text/tertiary` label, not
    interactive — matches (this one was a correct guess before the ticket was checked).
  - `radius/chip` (NOT `radius/sm` — corrected), `type/button` (14px Bold) label.
Same `iconPosition` convention as Secondary Button, so the two buttons feel like one family.

**2026-10-13 — changes from the Create position flow (Figma node 302:2265):**
  - **Height 52px.** Both Button instances in that flow (Create position, Save details) are
    52px tall per the frame's layout metadata; this component was ~32px (8px padding around
    a 16px icon). Applied as `min-height`. This reads as a change to SHO-12's locked spec —
    Figma wins (decision #23), but SHO-12 hasn't been updated in Linear.
  - **`loading` prop**, added at Shoham's request: the sync icon should turn while the fetch
    runs. Not in Figma — a new behavior, code-first. A continuous turn is `linear` per the
    `animate` skill (constant motion), and is dropped under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
  - **Hover is now gated** behind `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`. Un-gated `:hover` is
    sticky on touch: after one tap the button stayed in its darker Pressed color until the
    next tap elsewhere (installed `mobile-native` skill, §1). `:active` still gives press
    feedback on every input type.

`design-briefs/app-shell-states.md` §3.6 and canvas artboards 10–13, on top of

One sheet, two doors: the Archive action on the expanded card, and (later) the pull-down. The
design doc says only what is behind it and where focus returns differ — both are the
caller's, not the sheet's — so it takes no `entry` prop. Focus return is automatic: it goes

atoms-secondary-button.description:
Secondary Button (Linear SHO-32) — the "Subtle" variant of the unified Button component
in Figma (node 75:48, https://figma.com/design/q6vQcpCd8syg4YJPbdZj4D/...?node-id=75-48).
Pairs with Primary Button (SHO-12, same component, "Primary" variant — not yet translated,
not used by the Card). First use: the Card's "Show more details" CTA, which opens the same
Tap-in detail view as tapping the card's center (decision #16).

Added 2026-10-04: real Default / Pressed / Disabled interaction states, read directly off
node 75:48. That node exposes three "Subtle" states — in the Figma response they only come
back as "State4/State5/State6" (not resolved to real variant names by the design-context
tool), so the Default/Pressed/Disabled mapping below is inferred from left-to-right visual
order plus consistency with the "Primary" variant's own Default/Pressed/Disabled set, not a
literal name match — worth Shoham double-checking against the actual variant names in Figma.
  - Default:  border only, transparent fill                 (state "4")
  - Pressed:  border + color/accent/subtle-bg fill (#e3e1fb) (state "5")
  - Disabled: border + color/bg/surface-sunken fill (#e9ebef), non-interactive (state "6")
Per the Figma node's own code, label color does NOT change between these three states
(unlike the Primary variant, which dims its label on Disabled) — kept as-is here.

Outlined CTA, confirmed 2026-10-04 — Shoham added the border in Figma and matched the
label to type/button (14px Bold), closing the two drifts flagged during the initial
code translation. Border color is the same subtle token Logo Tile uses
(color/status-none/bg), reused deliberately, not a mismatch.

Fixed 2026-10-16 (found on a real iPhone, approved by Shoham): hover is now gated behind
`(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, default and danger variants. Un-gated `:hover` sticks
after a touch, so after a swipe the new top card's "Show more details" button showed the purple
pressed fill. `:active` still gives the pressed look on every device. Same fix PrimaryButton
already had. Confirmed by reading the CSS only; not yet seen on a device after the fix.

2026-09-22. Covers both the How Applied selector (Cold/Referred/Other) and, with only 2
segments shown, the Contact HR/Hiring Manager toggle (retires the separate Contact Toggle
Chip, SHO-11) — both uses needed by the Tap-in detail view (SHO-26).

`spacing/inline-gap` between segments. Figma models this as up to 4 fixed Segment Item
instances with boolean show/hide; in code that collapses to a plain `segments: string[]`
array (2–4 items) — same visual result, simpler API.

screens-stack.name: StackScreen
screens-stack.description:
Stack screen — built 2026-10-15 (app shell, phase A). Code-only: no Figma node; the design is
`design-briefs/app-shell-states.md` §3.1–3.3 and canvas artboards 01–03, with the layout rules
Shoham gave in comments on artboard 03 (briefs/app-shell.md §4).

It receives `records` as props and stores nothing. Header "Your stack" only (no count, no
"Steady week."), then the card deck, then the Bottom Nav with Stack current.

**Resting position.** The collapsed card rests centered between the header and the nav,
measured against a FIXED reference height (`--size-stack-card-reference`, 320px — was 280px until 2026-10-16) rather than
the card's own height, so every card's top edge is in the same place. In CSS, no JS: the
deck's top padding is `max(24px, (screen − header − nav − 320px) / 2)` to the card's top
edge (the Card's depth layers peek 16px above that). The screen's height is `100dvh`;
a parent can set `--stack-screen-height` to size it instead (the stories do).

**Expanding** grows the card downward only, its top edge fixed, with a height ease
(`--duration-base`, 220ms — the brief said "about 200ms"). There is no internal scroll box:
the page scrolls and the card moves up with it. The Bottom Nav is `sticky` at the bottom of
the screen, so it stays pinned while the page scrolls. While the height is easing the box
clips its bottom edge, so the card's shadow is cut off for those ~220ms. The ease runs on
expand AND collapse, but only the expand reads as an ease: the Card swaps its content
instantly, so on collapse the card is small at once and the space under it eases away.

**Browsing** is a horizontal swipe only; a tap on the card does nothing. It wraps last to
first; with one card it rubber-bands and returns. A swipe needs about 70px and to be mostly
horizontal. `touch-action: pan-y` leaves vertical scrolling native. Swiping to another card
remounts the Card (`key`), which collapses an expanded one, and scrolls the page back to the
top. Previous/Next buttons and a "Card n of m" status are the non-gesture path (design doc
§6); the buttons are visually hidden until one of them has keyboard focus (below). Reduced
motion: no slide, no rubber-band travel; the card just changes.

**Previous/Next revealed on keyboard focus (2026-10-16, Shoham approved after QA).** They used
to be a 1x1 clipped wrapper, so a sighted keyboard user tabbing onto one saw nothing. Now,
while either has focus (`:focus-within` on their group), both show as one row directly under
the "Your stack" header, absolutely positioned over the screen so nothing else shifts and the
card does not move. Each is the existing Secondary Button (reused, sized through `className`)
with a 16px Lucide ChevronLeft (leading) / ChevronRight (trailing), at least 44px tall
(`--size-touch-target`, new token). Unfocused, the group is clipped to nothing and has
`pointer-events: none`, so it can't swallow a tap meant for the card. They stay in the tab
order, Enter and Space still work (they are real buttons), and the reveal has no transition,
so reduced motion needs nothing special. Focusing one while the page is scrolled scrolls the
page to the top, because the row lives at the top — accepted by Shoham. Guessed: the row has a
`--color-bg-app` backing (the Secondary Button is transparent, so over the card it would be
unreadable) and an 8px gap to the header; neither was specified. `:focus-within` rather than
`:focus-visible` on the group, because the hidden buttons can't be reached by pointer anyway.

**Swipe reveals the card underneath (2026-10-16, Shoham's phone test: "it feels like you're
swiping the whole deck").** Before, the Card and its two depth layers moved as one block. Now,
for a COLLAPSED top card with 2+ records: past an 8px slop and mostly horizontal, only the top
card's wrapper (`data-stack-top`) follows the finger, 1:1, transform only. At that moment the
record that will become the top one (next for a left drag, previous for a right drag, wrapping;
it switches if the finger crosses back over the start point) is rendered in `data-stack-under`:
the true Card at the resting position (same box, so same top edge and width), below the face,
`aria-hidden`, `inert`, `pointer-events: none`, no scale or fade. The depth layers are the
underneath card's own, so they stay put; the moving face is rendered with `showDepthEffect`
off for the duration (the same layers, same pixels, so nothing jumps at drag start or end).
The Card component was not touched. Release: past 70px (unchanged), or a flick (at least 24px
and at least 0.5px/ms over the last 100ms, same direction), and mostly horizontal -> the face
flies the rest of the way off screen from where it is (`--duration-base`, `--ease-out`, at
least the screen width), then `commit()` changes the index. Both cards are keyed by record id
inside one parent, in a fixed order, so the underneath card's DOM node is kept and only moves
from the absolute slot into the flow: same pixels, no remount, no flicker. Otherwise the face
springs back. Input is ignored from release until the swap (`busy`), at most 220ms. The hidden
Previous/Next buttons use the same fly-out (Next = left). Under reduced motion the drag still
follows the finger (and the card underneath shows) but release, and the buttons, change the
card instantly. Unchanged on purpose: a single record rubber-bands the whole deck as before; an
EXPANDED card does not reveal anything (it has no depth layers and a different height) and keeps
the old behavior exactly, the whole deck sliding out and the next card sliding in, collapsing
as the Card remounts. `.screen` got `overflow-x: clip` so a flying card can't widen the page.
`will-change: transform` is set only while something moves. Known and left alone: the
underneath card is a true card, so one TALLER than the top card shows its extra height below
the top card from the first pixel of the drag (collapsed cards run 318-395px). Not yet seen on
a phone; the numbers (8px, 24px, 0.5px/ms) are guesses.

Not built here: persistence, the Archive action's sheet wiring, pull-down terminate, and
routing — `onNavigate`/`onAdd`/`onOpenArchive` are callbacks and nothing more.

Guesses, for review: the two empty states' layout follows the artboards' numbers
(block centered in the free area between the header's bottom edge and the nav's top edge —
the 24px top padding they were first built with was removed 2026-10-16, it put the block
12.5px low); the Toast's 16px-above-the-nav position is the brief's own proposal.

**2026-10-22, TEMPORARY: `onOpenBackupTemp`.** A mockup aid (Shoham: "we will not keep" it): the
home-screen app has no address bar, so the Backup page could not be reached. When passed,
`TempBackupLink` is drawn centred 16px below the empty state's buttons, in both empty states
only (as the brief says; never over the deck). It is part of the centred block, so the block's
centre moves up by half the link's height (about 30px), my call. Remove with the prop.

**2026-11-04, Add a step (Part B): follows the top card by id.** When the order of `records`
changes (adding a dated step moves its position to the front of the Stack), the deck keeps showing
the same card, at its new index, instead of keeping the old index and showing whichever card slid
into it. The Card is keyed by id, so it stays mounted and stays expanded: nothing jumps under her
thumb and no reorder animation plays. If the top card left the list (archived), the index behaves as
before.

molecules-step-chips.name: StepChips
molecules-step-chips.description:
Step Chips — a wrapping row of quick picks for the "Add a step" sheet (Add a step, Part B,
2026-11-04). Code-only: no Figma node, no Linear ticket (not checked).

The design brief flags that the system has NO home for a wrapping chip row (`SegmentedControl`
cannot wrap), and tells the builder to reuse its segment tokens and 44px height rather than invent
a style. So each chip is a segment look: `radius-pill`, the 13px label type, the accent-subtle
fill when selected (with a check, so it is not colour alone), at least `--size-touch-target`
tall, 12px (8 + 4, both tokens) of space each side as the scrollable segments have. Calls I
made: the chip sits on `color-bg-app` (the segment track's own colour) and its unselected text is
`color-text-secondary`, not the segments' tertiary (3.06:1 on white is too faint to read for a
tap target; that token is being darkened in a separate pass anyway); a long remembered name stops
at one line with an ellipsis; chips wrap with the 8px `spacing-inline-gap`.

Mark-done and remove sheet — Add a step, Part B (2026-11-04), from `design-briefs/stage-advance.md`
sections 2, 3, 5 and 8 and the copy file's section 5. On `ConfirmationSheet`. Code-only (no canvas
board or Linear ticket was opened).

Two modes. `mark` is what a planned row opens: title "<Label> happened?", When (today), "Mark as
done", "Not now", and "Remove this step" below the pair as a plain SecondaryButton (no red: the
system has no danger-link style). `remove` is what a done or upcoming row the app added opens:
title <Label>, the date as a line, only "Remove this step" and "Not now". A future date is allowed in

elsewhere, archived, gone, remove failed; archived and gone disable the actions ("Not now" is the
way out). A second press while one runs does nothing.

Calls I made (the briefs were silent): "Remove this step" is a SecondaryButton in both modes, with
no confirmation question (the design says Undo covers adding, and removing is reversible by adding
the step again); in `remove` mode "Not now" comes after it; no company line under the title (the
copy file lists none for these sheets).

atoms-text-input-field.name: TextInputField
atoms-text-input-field.description:
Text Input Field (Linear SHO-13) — confirmed built in Figma 2026-09-15 (marked Done), but
never translated to code until now. Built 2026-10-08, code-first per Shoham's call for this
Add flow pass (SHO-27).

SHO-13 turns out to carry a real locked spec, not just the "confirmed built" note
`visual-tokens.md` has — caught this only after an initial pass built from
`design-brief.md` + the token set alone guessed `radius/sm` and a `type/label` (13px) field
label; both were wrong. Corrected to match the ticket exactly: label is `type/caption`
(11.5px Bold, sentence case — not Section Label's small-caps treatment of the same token),
input is `radius/chip` (14px, not the Button components' `radius/sm`), height 52px fixed
(clears both iOS 44pt and Material 48dp touch-target minimums), horizontal padding
`spacing/section-gap` (16px). Border `color/border/default` → `color/accent/default` on
focus, `color/bg/surface` fill, `type/body` value text — all per the ticket's State =
Empty/Filled/Focused. No Error state exists yet (ticket says so explicitly), so this adds
none. Lesson for next time: pull the specific component ticket before building, not just the
screen-level one and the general design-brief/token docs.

**2026-10-13 — realigned to the "Input Field" instances in Figma node 302:2265** (the Create
position flow). Read directly off one of those instances (the How Applied field; the file's
Figma MCP quota ran out before the rest could be pulled, and every field in the flow is the
same named component): the label is `type/label` (13px Bold, `color/text/secondary`), NOT
SHO-13's `type/caption` — so SHO-13's label spec has been superseded by the newer Figma
build, which wins per decision #23 — and the label sits 4px (`space-4`) above the field, not
8. The instance also has a trailing icon slot, now `trailingIcon`. The field's 52px height,
14px radius, 16px padding and border were all re-confirmed unchanged. SHO-13 itself in
Linear has NOT been updated for this (connector still down) — flagged in the status doc.

First use: the Add flow's URL / Company / Role fields (design-brief.md §5).

**2026-10-15 — `multiline` variant** (app shell build, phase A), for the reason sheet's "A note
for later (optional)" field and, later, Notes (SHO-39). Shoham asked for it in a comment on
canvas artboard 10: three lines tall at minimum, growing as the person types (this reversed
the earlier "single-line for now" call). A prop, not a new component. CONFIRMED by that
comment: min height 96px, grows, no resize handle. FROM THE CANVAS ARTBOARDS (not Figma — no
node exists): 16px padding, the same border/radius/fill/label as the single-line field,
`rows=3`. GUESSED: growth is unbounded (the sheet it lives in scrolls instead), and a trailing
icon is not designed for this variant. The single-line field's look is untouched. Growth is
measured in JS (`scrollHeight`) because `field-sizing: content` isn't available everywhere
this runs.

**2026-10-25 — Edit position (Part B), additive props only.** `type` also takes `email`, `tel`
and `date`; new optional `inputMode`, `enterKeyHint`, `autoComplete`, `autoCapitalize`,
`autoCorrect`, `invalid` (strong border + `aria-invalid`), `describedBy`, `inputId`, `onBlur`,
`onEnter` and `trailingTouchTarget` (44px tap area on the trailing button, icon unmoved, via a negative
margin of `inline-gap + tight-gap` = 12px, which is half of 44 minus the 20px icon). From
`design-briefs/edit-position.md` sections 4, 9 and 10 (the "gap" they name). Without them
nothing changes: the Add screen renders as before. The `date` type is the browser's own date
input inside this chrome; not seen on a phone.

required.description:
Shows a "Required" tag next to the label — informational only, doesn't block typing.
Save-button gating (design-brief.md §5: "Save enabled once URL + Company + Role are
filled") is the caller's job, same as every other field-level validation in this app. The
2026-10-13 "Create position" frames show no Required tag at all, so that screen leaves
this off — the prop itself stays for any other use.

helperText.description:
Small text under the field — e.g. a fetch error, or a hint. Renders in the same tertiary
gray regardless of success/failure; no error/success color variant exists yet (same gap as
Signal Chip's missing per-state icon — flagged, not fixed, see the status doc).

inputMode.description:
Edit position (2026-10-25), all additive and optional: the keyboard and autofill hints the
Edit form needs (design-briefs/edit-position.md section 4). Absent, the input is exactly what
it was.

invalid.description:
Shows the invalid look (`color/border/strong` border) and sets `aria-invalid`. The words
explaining it are a NoteLine the caller puts under the field, linked with `describedBy`.

describedBy.description: `id` of the element that explains the field (a note under it), for `aria-describedby`.

inputId.description: Overrides the generated input id, so a screen can focus a field by id (first invalid field).

trailingTouchTarget.description: Makes the trailing button a 44px tap target (`size-touch-target`) without moving the icon.

onBlur.description: Called when the input loses focus (Edit: validation shows on blur, the draft is kept at once).

onEnter.description: Return pressed in a single-line field (Edit: moves to the next field, never saves).

multiline.description:
Multi-line variant (added 2026-10-15): a textarea at least 96px tall (three lines plus 16px
padding) that grows with its content, no manual resize handle. Same border, radius, fill,
label and touch-size rule as the single-line field. `type` is ignored when set.

trailingIcon.description:
Optional icon at the trailing edge of the field (the Figma Input Field's icon slot —
a clipboard on the URL field in the Create position flow).

onTrailingIconClick.description: Makes the trailing icon a real button. Without it the icon is decorative.

trailingIconLabel.description:
Accessible name for the trailing icon button — required in practice whenever
`onTrailingIconClick` is set, since an icon alone has no text.

atoms-toast.name: Toast
atoms-toast.description:
Toast (Linear SHO-19) — first translated to code 2026-10-15 (app shell, phase A), for the
first-run "Sample positions loaded. Swipe to look around." line.

CONFIRMED, read from the Toast component in Shoham's Paper file on 2026-10-15 (read-only;
130x28 for "Nice, moving up."): a pill, fill `color/text/primary`, text `color/text/on-dark`,
padding 4px 8px, 4px gap, Inter 14/600 line 1.4 (`type/body-strong`), `radius/pill`,
shrink-wrapping its text. NOT checked: SHO-19 itself in Linear (the connector isn't wired in
this environment), so a locked spec there could still differ.

**2026-10-20 (post-archive screen):** additive `action` and `announce` props, for the
snackbar `Archived · N in your stack` + `Done`. With an action the pill is at least 44px tall (the
action is a 44px tap target; the plain Toast stays 28px) and the text keeps its 16px start padding.
Without them the Toast is exactly what it was.

GUESSED / mine, not from the file: motion (opacity only — enter `--duration-base`, exit
`--duration-fast`, both `--ease-out`; none under `prefers-reduced-motion`); that it has no
position of its own (the Paper component has none — the consumer places it; the Stack puts it
16px above the Bottom Nav, centered, which is a proposal; with the 64px nav that is 80px from the screen's bottom, derived from the nav's height in StackScreen.module.css, not a literal); and `role="status"` (asked for).
It stays in the DOM while hidden, with `visibility: hidden` after the fade-out, so the live
region is persistent. Whether a given screen reader announces a status region that mounts
together with its text is not guaranteed — for a toast that must be heard, mount it empty
and set the message afterwards (not verified on a real device).

screens-unreadable-store.name: UnreadableStoreScreen
screens-unreadable-store.description:
Store unreadable screen — phase B step 2a (2026-10-19), from `design-briefs/app-shell-states.md`
§3.4 and canvas boards 04 to 07. The whole app shows this in place of Stack, Archive and Add
when the saved data can't be read; adding and archiving are paused because their writes would
overwrite the string. Nothing here writes: Copy reads, Try again re-reads, and Start fresh only
runs after the confirmation sheet and moves the string to a backup key (the caller's operation).

Copy is the design doc's, verbatim. States: default; Copied (the primary label, about 2s);
copy failed (the note above the buttons); try again, still unreadable (a note, "Nothing has
changed."); the Start fresh sheet. Added by me, not in the design doc: the line when there is
nothing to copy ("Nothing could be read, so there is nothing to copy."), and the note after a
Start fresh that failed ("Couldn't move the saved data aside. Nothing was changed."), both in
the same voice and slot as the designed notes. The title is the heading in the Stack's
header position (no separate "Your stack" header is drawn on boards 04 to 07). The nav stays so
nothing is a dead end. Not seen on a phone by the author.

copyText.description: The exact stored string, to copy.

copyable.description:
False when there is nothing to copy (storage could not be read, or the string is empty):
the Copy button is disabled and a line says why.

onTryAgain.description:
Re-reads the store. Returns true if it can be read now (the caller then replaces this
screen); false keeps this screen and shows "Still can't read it."

onStartFresh.description:
Moves the saved string to a backup key (the data layer's start-fresh). Returns true when it
worked. The sheet that asks first is this screen's.

defaultSheetOpen.description: Story convenience: start with the sheet open / a note showing.
